To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dietary fat composition is an important determinant of the fatty acid composition in the tissues and egg yolk of laying hens; the fatty acid composition is determined by the fatty acid pattern of the dietary fat and the fatty acid composition, in turn, affects the quality of the eggs and meat.
the fatty acid composition in egg yolk, liver and adipose tissue can be modified in laying hens by feeding different dietary oils.

the fatty acid composition in the liver, egg yolks and adipose tissue was generally proportional to the fatty acid pattern of dietary fats and the metabolic fate of individual FA from different fat sources were discussed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolic fate of individual dietary fatty acids and their interaction in laying hens fed various dietary fats.
a better understanding of the effect of dietary fats on the composition of tissue and egg yolks.
the effect of dietary fats on fatty acid composition and deposition in laying hens and the possible interaction of dietary fat on egg production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fatty acid composition in the tissue and egg yolks of laying hens can be modified by dietary fat sources.
the deposition of fatty acids in tissue and egg is dependent on the dietary fatty acid pattern, the metabolic activity of the animal and the metabolic fate of individual dietary fatty acids.

the fatty acid deposition is not simply a reflection of the fatty acid make up of dietary fat but is a complex function of dietary fat, dietary fatty acid, tissue fatty acid composition and the metabolic fate of the individual fatty acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary fat is an important factor in determining the fatty acid composition in the body fat and egg yolk of laying hens.
the fatty acid composition in the liver, adipose tissue, and egg yolk is affected by dietary fatty acid and the fatty acid composition and level of dietary fat.
animal tallow and low-fat diets were effective in reducing the level of unsaturated fatty acids in tissue and egg.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fatty acid make up of dietary fat has a profound effect on the fatty acid composition in tissue and egg.
the fatty acid composition in egg yolk, liver and adipose tissue can be altered by dietary manipulation.
the fatty acid composition can be modified in egg yolks and tissues by changing the dietary fatty acid composition.
